title: Deep Learning Basics: Exploring Neurons, Synapses, and Activation Functions

cues.en: Lecturer: Hello and welcome back to the course on Deep Learning.
cues.zh: 講師：大家好，歡迎回到深度學習。

cues.en: Today we're talking about the neuron, which is the basic building block of artificial neuron networks.
cues.zh: 今天談神經元，人工神經網路的基本單位。

cues.en: So let's get started.
Previously we saw an image which looked like this and these are actual real life neurons which have been smeared onto a glass and colored a little bit and they are observed through a microscope.
cues.zh: 先前看過這張圖，真實神經元塗到玻璃上，染色，用顯微鏡觀察。

cues.en: So this is what they look like, as you can see quite an interesting structure, a body, and then lots of different tails, kind of branches coming out of them.
cues.zh: 結構有趣，有細胞體，再有很多尾巴、分支。

cues.en: And this is very interesting, but the question is how can we recreate that in a machine?
cues.zh: 很有意思，但怎麼在機器重建？

cues.en: Because we really need to recreate that in a machine, since the whole purpose of deep learning is to mimic how the human brain works
cues.zh: 確實需要，因為深度學習目的是模仿人腦，

cues.en: in the hope that by doing so we are going to create something amazing.
We're gonna create an amazing infrastructure for machines to be able to learn.
cues.zh: 讓機器能學習的驚人基礎結構。

cues.en: And why do we hope for that?
Well, because the human brain is, well just happens to be one of the most powerful learning tools on the planet or like learning mechanisms on the planet.
cues.zh: 因為人腦恰好是地球最強學習工具、機制之一。

cues.en: And we just hope that if we recreate that we'll have something as awesome as that.
cues.zh: 希望重建後，也有如此厲害的東西。

cues.en: So our challenge right now, our very first step to creating artificial neural networks is to recreate a neuron.
cues.zh: 現在挑戰、建立 ANN 第一步，是重建神經元。

cues.en: So how do we do that?
Well, first of all let's have a closer look at what it actually is.
cues.zh: 先仔細看它實際是什麼。

cues.en: This image was first created by Spanish neuroscientist Santiago Ramon y Cajal in 1899.
cues.zh: 這幅圖由西班牙神經科學家 Santiago Ramón y Cajal 於 1899 年畫。

cues.en: And what he did was he dyed neurons in actual brain tissue and looked at them under a microscope.
cues.zh: 把真實腦組織神經元染色，顯微鏡下看。

cues.en: And while he was looking at them he actually drew what he saw.
And this is what he saw.
He saw two neurons or two large neurons over there at the top, which had all these branches coming out of them towards their top parts.
cues.zh: 上方兩個大神經元，上部伸出所有這些分支。

cues.en: And then each one of them had this rod or like thread coming out towards the bottom.
cues.zh: 各有一條桿子、細線往下。

cues.en: Very long one.
And yeah, so that's what he saw.
And now, technology has advanced quite a lot and we have seen neurons much closer in more detail and now we can actually draw what it looks
cues.zh: 現在技術進步很多，更近、更詳細看過神經元，能畫出

cues.en: like diagrammatically.
So let's have a look at that.
Here's a neuron.
This is what it looks like.
Very similar to what Santiago Ramon drew over here.
cues.zh: 很像 Santiago Ramón 這裡畫的。

cues.en: And here in this neuron, what we can see is that it's got a body, well that's the main part of the neuron, and then it's got some branches at the top which are called dendrites, and it's also got an axon
cues.zh: 有細胞體，主要部分；上方分支叫樹突，還有軸突，

cues.en: which is that long tail of the neuron.
And so what are these dendrites and what's the axon for?
Well, the key point to understand here is that neurons by themselves are pretty much useless.
cues.zh: 關鍵是，單個神經元基本無用。

cues.en: It's like an an right, an on its own can't do much like five ants together maybe they can pick something up but again, they can't build an ant hill,
cues.zh: 像螞蟻，一隻做不了多少，五隻也許搬東西，但不能造蟻丘、

cues.en: they can't establish a colony.
They can't work together as a huge organism.
cues.zh: 不能像大型生物一起運作。

cues.en: But at the same time, when you have lots and lots of ants like you have a million ants, they can build a whole colony.
cues.zh: 但很多很多，例如一百萬隻，就能建整個群落。

cues.en: They can build an ant hill.
Same thing with neurons, by itself it's not that strong but when you have lots of neurons together they work together to do magic.
cues.zh: 神經元一樣，單個不強，很多一起就能創造奇蹟。

cues.en: And how do they work together?
That's the question.
Well, that's what the dendrites and the axon are for.
So the dendrites are kind of like the receivers of the signal for the neuron.
And the axon is the transmitter of the signal for the neuron.
And here's an image of how it all works conceptually.
So at the top you've got a neuron and you can see that it's dendrites are connected to axons of other neurons that are like even further away above it.
cues.zh: 上方神經元的樹突，連接更上方其他神經元的軸突。

cues.en: And then the signal from this neuron travels down its axon and connects or passes onto the dendrites of the next neuron.
cues.zh: 訊號沿軸突向下，連到、傳給下一個樹突。

cues.en: And that's how they're connected.
And in that small image over there, you can see that the axon doesn't actually touch the dendrites.
cues.zh: 小圖可見軸突其實不碰樹突。

cues.en: A lot of machine learning or like a few machine learning scientists are very adamant about the fact that it doesn't touch,
cues.zh: 一些機器學習科學家很堅持這點，沒有接觸，

cues.en: it doesn't touch, it has been proven that there is no physical connection there.
cues.zh: 已證實沒有直接物理連接。

cues.en: But the point that we are interested in is that, that connection between them, the whole concept of the signal being passed, that's called the synapse.
cues.zh: 但我們關心兩者連結、訊號傳遞概念，叫突觸。

cues.en: You can see over there in that little image that figure bracket is a synapse.
cues.zh: 小圖大括號標示就是突觸。

cues.en: And that's the term we're going to be using.
So instead of calling our artificial neurons, the lines that we're gonna have or the connectors for artificial neurons, we're not gonna be calling them axons or dendrites
cues.zh: 所以人工神經元之間的線、連接器，不叫軸突或樹突，

cues.en: because then the question is, whose connection is this?
cues.zh: 不然會問這是誰的連結？

cues.en: Is it that neurons or is it this neurons?
We just going to call them synapses and that kind of just answers all questions right away.
cues.zh: 直接叫突觸，回答所有問題。

cues.en: That's just basically where the signal is passed, doesn't matter who that element belongs to.
cues.zh: 基本上就是訊號傳遞處，不論元素歸誰。

cues.en: So that's just a representation of the signal being passed.
And we'll see that just now.
So basically that's how a neuron works.
And yeah, so let's move on to how we going to represent neurons or how create neurons in machines.
cues.zh: 接著看機器如何表示、建立神經元。

cues.en: So we're moving away from neuroscience and moving into technology.
And here we go.
So here's our neuron also sometimes called the node.
The neuron gets some input signals and it has an output signal.
cues.zh: 收到輸入訊號，產生輸出訊號。

cues.en: So dendrites and axons, remember, but again we're gonna call these synapses.
cues.zh: 記得樹突、軸突，但都叫突觸。

cues.en: Then these input signals, we're gonna represent them with other neurons as well.
cues.zh: 輸入訊號也用其他神經元表示。

cues.en: So in this specific case, you can see that this neuron this green neuron is getting signals from yellow neurons.
cues.zh: 這例綠色從黃色接收訊號。

cues.en: And in this course we're going to try and stick to a certain color coding regime where yellow means an input layer.
cues.zh: 本課盡量維持配色，黃色代表輸入層。

cues.en: So basically all of the neurons that are on the outer layer or in the first front of where the signal's coming in.
cues.zh: 最外層、訊號進來第一線的神經元。

cues.en: And by signal it might be a bit of an overkill to call this a signal.
It's just basically input values.
So you know how even like in a simple linear regression you have input values and then you have a predicted value.
cues.zh: 像簡單線性迴歸，有輸入、預測值。

cues.en: Same thing here.
So you have input values and there they are the yellow ones.
And then on the right you'll see just now it'll be red, it'll be the output value.
cues.zh: 右邊等一下紅色，是輸出。

cues.en: The thing that I wanted to point out here is that in this specific example, we're looking at a neuron which is getting its signals from the input layer neurons.
cues.zh: 想指出，這例神經元接收輸入層的訊號。

cues.en: So they're also neurons but they're input layer neurons.
cues.zh: 它們也是神經元，但屬輸入層。

cues.en: Sometimes you'll have neurons which get their signal from other hidden layer neurons.
cues.zh: 有時也接其他隱藏層神經元訊號。

cues.en: So from other green neurons.
And the concept is gonna be exactly the same.
It's just in this case, for simplicity sake we're portraying this example.
And in terms of the input layer the way to think about it is in the analogy of the human brain, the input layer is your senses, right?
cues.zh: 人腦比喻裡，輸入層就是感官。

cues.en: So whatever you can see here, feel, touch or smell.
cues.zh: 看到、聽到、感覺、觸碰、聞到。

cues.en: And of course it's like there's a lot of things you can see.
There's a lot of information coming in, but that's what your brain is limited to.
cues.zh: 大量資訊，但腦只能靠這些。

cues.en: It pretty much lives in a box made out of bones.
And it's a mind blowing concept to think about, that your brain is just locked in a black box.
cues.zh: 想想腦被關黑盒，非常驚人。

cues.en: Like you can't see, you can't hear the only thing it's getting is electrical impulses coming from these organs that you have which are called your ears, nose, eyes,
cues.zh: 自己看不見、聽不到，只接收耳、鼻、眼等器官來的電脈衝，

cues.en: your sense of touch and what whatever and your taste, right?
So it's just getting signals, but it basically lives in this dark black box and it's making sense of the world through your senses.
cues.zh: 只收到訊號，住在黑暗盒子，透過感官理解世界。

cues.en: It's phenomenal.
And so you have these inputs that are coming in, in the terms of human brain, those are your five senses.
And in terms of machine learning or deep learning that is basically your input values.
cues.zh: 機器或深度學習則基本是輸入值。

cues.en: So your independent variables and we'll get to that in a second.
So your input values, the signal is passed through synapses to the neuron and then your neuron has an output value that it passes further on down the chain.
cues.zh: 輸入經突觸到神經元，再產生輸出，往下傳。

cues.en: In this specific case in terms of color-coding, again, yellow means input layer.
So we're kind of simplifying everything here.
We're saying we're only gonna have the input layer then we're gonna have one hidden layer with the green which is the hidden layer.
cues.zh: 只有輸入層、一個綠色隱藏層，

cues.en: And then we're gonna have the output layer right away.
Just so that we can get used to these colors for now.
So there we go.
That's the basic structure.
So now let's look in a bit more detail at these different elements that we have.
So we've got the input layer, and what do we have here?
Well, we have these inputs which are in fact independent variables.
So independent variable one, independent variable two independent variable m.
The important things to remember here is that these independent variables are all for one single observation.
cues.zh: 重要的是，都屬單一觀測。

cues.en: So think of it as just one row in your database.
One observation, you just take all of the independent variables, maybe it's the age of the person, the amount of money in the bank accounts,
cues.zh: 一筆觀測，取全部自變數，例如年齡、銀行存款，

cues.en: and then how do they drive or walk to work?
What method of transportation do they use?
But that's all descriptors of one specific person that you are either training your model on or you're performing some prediction on.
cues.zh: 全描述某位特定的人，用來訓練或預測。

cues.en: And the other thing you need to know about these variables is that you need to standardize them.
So you need to either standardize them which means make sure that they have a mean of zero and variance one, or you can also sometimes and (indistinct) point out these situations
cues.zh: 可標準化，確保平均 0、變異數 1；有時 Hadelin 會詳細指出

cues.en: in a bit more detail.
Perhaps in the practical tutorials you might come across these, sometimes you might want to not standardize you might wanna normalize them, meaning that instead of making sure the mean and zero
cues.zh: 實作可能遇到，有時不標準化，而是正規化；不要求平均 0、

cues.en: variance is one, you just subtract the minimum value and then you divide by the maximum minus minimum sum by the range of your values, and before you get values between zero and one.
cues.zh: 變異數 1，而是減最小值，再除最大減最小，也就是範圍，得到 0 到 1。

cues.en: And it depends on the scenario.
You might wanna do one or the other but basically you want all of these variables to be quite similar, about the same range of values.
cues.zh: 可能選其一，但基本希望變數類似、大約相同範圍。

cues.en: And why is that?
Well, all of these values are going to go into a neural network where as we'll see just now they'll be added up and multiply by way it's added up and so on.
cues.zh: 全部進網路，等一下看到會乘權重、相加等等。

cues.en: And just going to be easier for the neural network to process them if they're all about the same.
cues.zh: 範圍接近，網路比較易處理。

cues.en: And in fact, that's just how it is going to be able to work properly.
cues.zh: 事實上這樣才能正常工作。

cues.en: And if you want to read more about standardization normalization and other things that you can do with your input variables.
cues.zh: 若想深入標準化、正規化與其他輸入處理，

cues.en: A good additional reading paper is called "Efficient Backprop" by Yann LeCun 1998, the links over there.
cues.zh: 好讀物是 Yann LeCun 1998 年 Efficient Backprop，連結在這。

cues.en: So Yann LeCun, we're actually going to talk more about this phenomenal person in the space of deep learning in the part of the course where you're talking
cues.zh: 卷積神經網路部分會多談這位

cues.en: about convolution neural networks.
And you'll see that this is definitely a person who knows what he's talking about.
cues.zh: 會看到他確實了解自己在說什麼。

cues.en: He's a close friend of Jeffrey Hinton who we've already seen, who've already mentioned.
cues.zh: 也是已提過的 Geoffrey Hinton 好友。

cues.en: So in this paper you'll learn more about standardization and normalization but also you can pick up lots of other different tips and tricks and he'll be a good source
cues.zh: 論文介紹標準化、正規化，也能學很多其他技巧，是課程中

cues.en: for additional reading as you go through this course.
So definitely check it out if you're interested in.
So yeah, check it out if you are interested in some additional reading.
There we go.
So that's what we need to do with the variables.
And here we've got the output value.
So what can our output value be?
Well, we've got a couple options.
Well, we've got a couple of options.
Output value can be, it can be continuous.
Like for instance, price, it can be binary.
For instance, a person will exit or will stay or it can be a categorical variable.
cues.zh: 例如某人離開或留下，或類別變數。

cues.en: And if it's a categorical variable the important thing to remember here is that in that case your output value won't be just one it'll be several output values
cues.zh: 若類別，要記得不只一個輸出，而是多個，

cues.en: because these will be your dummy variables which will be representing your categories.
And that just how it works.
And just important to remember that in that case that's how you're going to be getting your categories out of the artificial neural network.
cues.zh: 記得這是從 ANN 取得類別的方法。

cues.en: But let's go back to a simple case of one output value.
cues.zh: 但回到單一輸出的簡單例。

cues.en: One more point or kind of like another point that we've already made.
I just wanted to reiterate this point.
On the left, you've got a single observation.
So one of your data set and on the right you have a single observation as well.
cues.zh: 資料集一列，右邊也單一觀測。

cues.en: And that is the same observation.
So important to remember that whatever inputs you're putting in, that's for one row and then the output you get that is for that same exact row.
cues.zh: 輸入屬一列，輸出也完全同列。

cues.en: Or if you're training you're neural network then you're putting the inputs in for that one row you're putting the output in for that one row.
cues.zh: 訓練時，輸入與輸出也都同一列。

cues.en: So if you wanna simplify the complexity think of it as a, like a simple linear regression or a multivariate linear regression.
cues.zh: 想簡化複雜度，就像簡單或多變數線性迴歸。

cues.en: So you're putting in your values you have your output, there's no question about it, when were talking about things like regression because we're so used to it, same thing here.
cues.zh: 輸入值、有輸出，談迴歸很習慣不會疑問，這裡相同。

cues.en: It's nothing too complex.
We're just putting in values, we're getting output.
But just remember that every time it's one row you're dealing with.
So you don't get confused and start putting in, thinking that these are different rows that you're putting into your artificial neural network or something.
cues.zh: 別混淆，以為輸入 ANN 的是不同列。

cues.en: This is all just values in that one row.
So different observation, different characteristics or attributes relating to that one observation every single time.
cues.zh: 每次都是同一觀測的不同特徵或屬性。

cues.en: Okay, so next thing that we want to talk about here is the or is the synapses.
Here we've got synapses and they all actually get assigned weights.
Weights, we're gonna talk more about weights for the down.
But in short, weights are crucial to our artificial neural networks functioning because weights are how
cues.zh: 簡單說很關鍵，因為神經網路是透過

cues.en: neural networks learn by adjusting the weights.
The neural network decides in every single case what signal is important, what signal is not important to a certain neuron.
cues.zh: 網路在各情況決定，對某神經元哪些訊號重要、哪些不重要。

cues.en: What signal gets passed along and what signal doesn't get passed along, or to what strength, to what extent signals get passed along.
cues.zh: 哪些傳、哪些不傳，或傳多強、多大程度。

cues.en: So weights are crucial.
They are the things that get adjusted through the process of learning.
cues.zh: 學習過程調整的就是它們。

cues.en: Like when you're training out into artificial neural network, you're basically adjusting all of the weights in all the synapses across this whole neural network.
cues.zh: 訓練 ANN，基本上調整整個網路全部突觸權重。

cues.en: And that's where gradient descent and back propagation come into play.
cues.zh: 梯度下降、反向傳播在此發揮作用。

cues.en: And those are concepts that we'll also discuss.
So basically those are the weights.
That's all we need to know for now.
And here we've got the neurons.
So signals go into the neuron and what happens in the neuron.
So this is the interesting part, like we're talking about the neuron today.
What happens inside the neuron?
So a few things happen, first thing and the first step is that all of these values that it's getting get added up.
cues.zh: 幾件事，第一把所有收到的值加總。

cues.en: So it takes the added, so the weighted sum of all of the input values that it's getting.
cues.zh: 取所有輸入值的加權和。

cues.en: Very simple, right?
It's very, very straightforward.
Just add up, multiply by the weight, add them up.
And then it applies an activation function.
Now we're gonna talk more about activation functions further down but it's basically a function that is assigned to this neuron or to this whole layer
cues.zh: 稍後多談，基本上是指定給神經元或整層的函數，

cues.en: and it is applied to this weighted sum.
And then from that, the neuron understands if it needs to pass on a signal, that's the signal that it passes on,
cues.zh: 神經元藉此知道是否傳訊號，輸出就是

cues.en: the function applied to the weighted sum.
cues.zh: 函數作用於加權和的結果。

cues.en: But basically depending on the function, the neuron will either pass on a signal or it won't pass the signal on.
cues.zh: 根據函數，可能傳或不傳。

cues.en: And that's exactly what happened here in step three, the neuron passes on that signal to the next neuron down the line.
cues.zh: 第三步正如此，傳給下一個神經元。

cues.en: And that's what we're going to talk about in the next tutorial because it is quite an important topic.
We want to delve deeper into the activation function but hopefully for now, everything is should be pretty clear how you've got input values, you've got weights
cues.zh: 想深入活化函數；目前希望都清楚，有輸入值、權重、

cues.en: you've got the synapses you've got something that happens in the neuron you've got the weighted sum and then activation functions applied and then that is paused down the line.
cues.zh: 突觸、神經元內部加權和，套活化函數，再往下傳。

cues.en: And that is just repeated throughout the whole neural network.
On and on and on and on.
Thousands, hundreds of thousands of times depending on how big, how many neurons you have how many synapses as you have in your neural network.
cues.zh: 數千、數十萬次，取決大小、神經元與突觸數。

cues.en: So there we go.
Hope you enjoyed today's tutorial.
Can't wait to see you next time.
And until then, enjoy deep learning.
cues.zh: 在那之前，祝你享受深度學習的樂趣。
